# Native underwater rock at original 7|6

This fixture retains the complete Request 3 failure from the 2.9.162 live test.
`rock-effect.png` is the byte-original final capture; `before-match.png` is the
byte-original first unmatched capture, with the actual 5H still present at 7|6.
`deal.json` is the packet's original complete deal, read through xSAR's strict
`pyramid_json::read_from` codec. SHA256 values are recorded in `calibration.json`.

The pending second operation was MATCH(5H at original 7|6, 8C at DL). Its expected
result retains all original card identities, marks original indices 21, 23 and
26 Empty, and expects DL = 3C and DR = Empty. The earlier completed operation
removed 5S at 7|1 and 8S at 7|3. The recorded execution diagnostic was
`execution slot 26 lacks positive absence`.

`underwater-rock-clearance.rgb` contains every RGB channel from the final PNG's
fixed native rectangle `(1289,588,144,34)`: 4,896 pixels, 14,688 bytes, row-major
with RGB channel order. It supplies a separate exact absence proof only at
original one-based 7|6, after strong-white presence and before generic aged-colour
refusal. There are no masked pixels, adjustable tolerances or additional
references. The existing 7|1 Coral structural proof remains separate.

The final rock probe has 65/240 aged-colour pixels and its clearance has
1,510/4,896. Bare rock therefore exceeds the generic material limits. The exact
proof intentionally recognises the complete retained artwork; it does not change
those material predicates or establish that the generic reader recognises rock.

The first unmatched frame is historical evidence and retains the pending cards.
Its early scene mismatch must not be mistaken for the final capture's cause.
The retained final pixels are consistent with removal and DL advancement, but do
not independently prove guest credit. Full-position regression success on this
calibration frame is offline evidence. Future appearance coverage, the rendering
cause and fresh live guest acceptance remain unproven.

The regressions verify the complete post-MATCH position and immutable pixels,
crop provenance, real surviving-card refusal, full and partial material overlays,
zero-tolerance channel changes including the last pixel, shifted artwork,
fixed-slot restrictions, identities, both piles, scene support and checked layout.
